---
title: "Inventory on Start + Void"
description: "Inventory Worker identity, acceptance commands, smoke checks and Vercel rollback packet."
updatedAt: "2026-11-09"
audience: developers
---

Inventory (`apps/inventory`) runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void with the
shared Start bridge. Its native Worker owns `inventory.tuturuuu.com`; the source
configuration declares no routes and the release operator attaches the host.
Production publication remains held until exact-head CI, sealed emitted-Worker
acceptance, staging acceptance and rollback capture pass. Vercel remains
available as the rollback target through cutover.

## Cutover packet

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Production Worker | `tuturuuu-inventory` (`VITE_INVENTORY_NATIVE_PROFILE=production`) |
| Staging Worker | the staging Worker name |
| Host | `inventory.tuturuuu.com` (operator-attached; no source route) |
| Bindings and vars | `ASSETS` (`dist/client`), `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX` (`0` production, `1` staging) |
| Secret names | `CRON_SECRET`, `SEPAY_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID`, `SEPAY_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, `SEPAY_OAUTH_STATE_SECRET`, `SEPAY_OAUTH_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_SECRET`, `ENCRYPTION_MASTER_KEY`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN`, `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, and one of `SEPAY_WEBHOOK_API_KEY` or `SEPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| Build | `VITE_INVENTORY_NATIVE_PROFILE=production bun run --cwd apps/inventory build:cloudflare` |
| Prior Vercel deployment | No immutable deployment ID is recorded in the repository. Rex must capture the active Inventory Vercel deployment ID and URL before cutover. |
| Data | Checkout-expiry acceptance uses disposable reservations. The routing and scheduler handoff requires no schema migration. |

## Acceptance and smoke

Run the production build and emitted suite from the repository root:

```bash
VITE_INVENTORY_NATIVE_PROFILE=production bun run --cwd apps/inventory build:cloudflare
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" bun run --cwd apps/inventory test:runtime
```

After the release owner deploys the accepted artifact and attaches the host:

```bash
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://inventory.tuturuuu.com/
curl -sS https://inventory.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://inventory.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
```

Confirm expected page/auth behavior, the exact accepted source SHA in build
info, and `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native`. Smoke the canonical subdomain and the
`https://tuturuuu.com/inventory` mount if it is admitted by the cutover. This
packet does not authorize routing or provider changes.

## Move checkout expiry to Cron Control

Before the Inventory cutover, transfer `inventory-checkout-expiry` to the
existing `tuturuuu-cron-control` Worker at `*/5 * * * *`. Select the job in
both `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS` and `CRON_CONTROL_WORKER_PROCESSORS` to run
the Worker processor. The legacy HTTP `GET` processor shares the database
claim, while Cron Control's durable stop fence covers its own dispatch.
Switch owners between slots and drain the former owner before starting the next.

1. Capture the current Vercel deployment, schedule state, and last checkout-expiry
   run. Capture the Cron Control deployment, trigger, selector, and ledger state.
   Confirm the Worker has `CRON_SECRET_INVENTORY` and the target Inventory host
   accepts it for the bounded `POST /api/cron/inventory/checkout-expiry` adapter.
   Use binding names and test receipts in the release record.
2. Prove the Worker processor against a disposable reservation and storefront in
   the hosted test environment. Confirm a single `reserved` → expired transition,
   a rejected duplicate slot, and a positive per-workspace revalidation receipt.
   Verify the storefront read on its serving host. A native Inventory response
   cannot invalidate a cache on the retained Next.js deployment.
3. Stop the hosted test job through the authenticated
   `POST /control/jobs/inventory-checkout-expiry/stop` endpoint. Observe the next
   due slot skip processor work and verify the stop survives a restart. Reconcile
   any expiry RPC that might have committed before the revalidation obligation was
   recorded. Review pending and quarantined obligations before resuming.
4. In the authorized production handoff, disable the Vercel schedule and confirm
   its last invocation has completed. Activate the Cloudflare job with the Worker
   processor selected. Verify a successful slot, the expired count, storefront
   freshness, and subsequent slots with Cloudflare as the sole scheduler.
5. Remove the checkout-expiry entry from `apps/inventory/vercel.json` and remove
   its backend-ownership allowlist entry. Verify the Vercel schedule is absent in
   provider readback before releasing the Inventory routes. Keep the authenticated
   `POST` adapter for Cron Control's follow-up work.

The processor runs once per slot. It caps expiry at ten batches of 1,000 rows,
uses a 240-second deadline within a 270-second lease, and revalidates in chunks of
100 workspaces. The database claims only reserved rows. A SQLite Durable Object
persists the slot, stop state, and follow-up obligations. Verify these bounds,
retry and quarantine behavior, and the stop fence in the existing processor and
dispatch tests. See [the processor runbook](/build/devops/cloudflare-processor-migration).

## Rollback

Before switching, Rex records the active Vercel deployment ID, immutable URL,
and routing it serves. If smoke, authentication, error rate or latency regresses,
restore the captured host routing to that Vercel deployment in one step; do not
rebuild during rollback. Retain the Vercel deployment and routing until the
native Worker completes its stable release window.

If checkout expiry regresses, stop the Cron Control job and reconcile the last
slot and outstanding revalidations before resuming. A route rollback to Vercel
keeps Cron Control as the scheduler. Confirm that its authenticated revalidation
callback reaches the Inventory deployment serving the storefront reads.
